confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from six web searches that mostly returned aggregator pages (Traveltables, dated July 2023), sample menus and travel blogs. They were not current, standardised Interlaken price indexes. Sources gave a cappuccino at about CHF 4-6 and a draught beer at about CHF 7-8, while the Interlaken inexpensive-meal figure is a roughly $27 estimate from 2023. The mid-range two-person meal drew on a 2023 figure of about $115 and a 2026 per-person estimate of roughly EUR 44, then I adjusted up for peak July tourist pricing. No Interlaken-specific cocktail or wine-by-the-glass price was found. Cocktail is based on a Swiss estimate of CHF 15-20 and a travel-guide range of $12-15. Wine is based on the local-beer price, plus a roughly CHF 7-9 glass assumption from general knowledge. The CHF to USD conversion of about 1.25 was my own assumption and was not searched. Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge of Interlaken's peak-season pricing. I did not search accommodation prices or inspect any listings. Hostel, 1-star and 3-star July rates are the least certain anchors, because peak-season and booking-timing variation is large.
comparable_city_reasoning: Interlaken is a high-cost Swiss alpine tourist hub. Prices are set against Swiss price levels, as in Zurich and Lucerne, with a small premium or discount for a smaller town. July is peak season, so accommodation is priced above the annual average.
